 11h ago 07.07 EST That’s all from me today. Join us for minute-by-minute coverage of Arsenal v London City Lionesses at 4:30pm and Spain v England at 7:45pm.
 Share 11h ago 07.07 EST Is Andy Robertson Scotland’s best captain? Check out Ewan Murray’s read.
 Record-breaking Andy Robertson is Scotland’s finest captain Read more Share 12h ago 06.54 EST 
 double quotation mark It’s not a must-win game if you go to Spain. But the mindset is important. Beating Croatia so we could have this match was the first step and now it’s important that we play with the same mindset that we played at home [against Spain] – attack them, try to make it a physical game, impose our strength. And we will. I’m very confident about that.
 View image in fullscreen Thomas Tuchel wants England to take the game to Spain. Photograph: Eddie Keogh/The FA/Getty Images Share 12h ago 06.44 EST Back on the pitch, Tuchel is as focused as ever on tonight’s test. The Nations League can be a springboard into the Euros and there’s no better test than a match against the world champions.
 ‘No one is unbeatable’: Tuchel eager for England to impose style on Spain Read more Share 12h ago 06.30 EST The whole row seems to be manufactured as England have played three times in Spain without incident since 2004. Nonetheless, Luis de la Fuente’s claim that “there is no racism in Spain” seems pretty ridiculous after Spain’s football federation were fined for discriminatory chants about Muslims during their game against Egypt in March. That’s before we mention the racism that La Liga stars Vinícius Júnior and Lamine Yamal have publicly spoken out about over the years.
 Share 12h ago 06.18 EST Luis de la Fuente has insisted that is no racism in Spain in response to Thomas Tuchel’s comments about anti-racism protocol. This evening’s game at the Metropolitano will be the first time England and Spain play against each other in Madrid since some of England’s black players were subjected to racist abuse at the Santiago Bernabéu in 2004. When asked about this incident, Tuchel said that England “will not expect anything [untoward]” to happen today. He added: “Maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent.”
 De la Fuente adamant there is no racism in Spain despite England reminder to players Read more Share 12h ago 06.05 EST Lamine Yamal and Mikel Oyarzabal did not join the Spain squad in Prague for their 2-0 win over Czechia on Thursday. According to Spain’s manager Luis de la Fuente, Lamine Yamal was omitted due to some discomfort in his knee. But that didn’t stop Spanish media outlets from arguing that the Barcelona winger was receiving preferential treatment. Read Sid Lowe’s report about the club v country debate here.
 De la Fuente feels the strain as Lamine Yamal club v country debate rages in Spain Read more Share 13h ago 05.51 EST Harry Kane also described today’s game as “the perfect opportunity to prove ourselves.” The Ballon d’Or winner has proved himself repeatedly and will need to do the same against a Spain side that will surely welcome the Kopa award winner Lamine Yamal back to the squad.
 View image in fullscreen Lamine Yamal finished third in a Ballon d’Or race which saw Harry Kane scoop the top prize. Photograph: Ben Gregory-Ring/PA Share Updated at  05.52 EST 13h ago 05.32 EST 
 double quotation mark By my standards it was an average World Cup. France was probably my best game, Congo I played really well; some of the other games I didn’t play too well but you look back … I played 69 games [in the season].
 A title win with Arsenal, a Champions League final loss and into a World Cup. It’s annoying because at the World Cup you want to be at your best, you want to be totally fresh, you want to be ready. It’s annoying that I couldn’t perform how I did at Arsenal towards the back end of the season.
 But knowing if I’m not going to be at my best, just constantly give 100% for this team, for the badge and you could see that. I loved [the last-16 win in] Mexico. We had the disappointment of Argentina in the semi-final, the second group game against Ghana. It’s games you look back on and think: ‘Could I have done better?
 View image in fullscreen Declan Rice was frustrated with some of his performances at the World Cup. Photograph: Óscar del Pozo/AFP/Getty Images Share 13h ago 05.27 EST One of the players who will be most keen to impress is Declan Rice. After an “average” World Cup, he took some time out to return stronger for club and country. Read David Hytner’s piece here.
 Declan Rice accepts he had an ‘average World Cup’ as England gear up for Spain showdown Read more Share 13h ago 05.12 EST Turning our attention back to the Nations League, England play Spain at 7:45pm. It’s an important game for England, who feel as though they have something to prove after their World Cup semi-final exit against Argentina and their 3-2 defeat against Spain two months ago. What will the score be today? Email me with your predictions.
 Share 14h ago 04.59 EST The tables have turned heading into today’s game at The Emirates. Arsenal have won all seven of their meetings with London City Lionesses in all competitions, scoring 22 and conceding only one. Despite that, the home side languish three places and six points behind an impressive London City Lionesses side this season. Who do you think will win today’s game?

 We have a huge derby day today. John Brewin will provide you with minute-by-minute coverage of Arsenal v London City Lionesses at 4:30pm.

 Share 14h ago 04.37 EST Japan’s head coach Hajime Moriyasu said that his side could “become the world’s best” at future World Cups after they beat Brazil 3-2 in a friendly. Japan went 2-0 up before Vinícius Júnior brought things level with a brace. A late goal from Tatsuhiro Sakamoto gave Japan the victory and enraged Carlo Ancelotti and Raphinha in the process, with both individuals receiving red cards as they protested against the goal. Read the roundup from yesterday’s friendlies here.
 Raphinha sees red as Brazil stunned by Japan while Argentina’s post-Messi era starts with defeat Read more Share 14h ago 04.18 EST Away from the Nations League, there was a huge game between Chelsea and Manchester City in the Women’s Super League yesterday. A belter from Sandy Baltimore saw Sonia Bompastor’s side leapfrog last year’s WSL champions in the table. Read Suzanne Wrack’s match report here.

 Share 14h ago 04.07 EST Elsewhere, Jamaica pulled off a historic upset, beating Mexico 3-2 in the first leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final. The home side led 3-0 midway through the second half before Mexico clawed two goals back through Gilberto Mora and Julián Quiñones. Mexico are winless in five games, under new manager Rafael Márquez, with Jamaica needing a draw to advance to the next stage of the competition.
 View image in fullscreen Jamaica’s surprise 3-2 win over Mexico extends Rafael Márquez’s winless run to five games, one of the worst managerial starts in the history of the Mexican national team. Photograph: Collin Reid/AP Share Updated at  04.31 EST 15h ago 03.57 EST Fernandes says Portugal thrashing was 'a night of learning'
 double quotation mark There are no nights to forget; it was a night of learning, of seeing the mistakes we made. Denmark were also very clinical – they scored from the chances they had and it was a match where things ultimately went wrong for us.
 View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes talks to the media after Portugal’s 4-1 defeat by Denmark. Photograph: Diogo Cardoso/Uefa/Getty Images Share Updated at  04.10 EST 15h ago 03.54 EST Portugal suffered a huge defeat against Denmark in their first game back after Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football. Rasmus Højlund scored a brace as Denmark eased their way to victory to a chorus of boos in Estadio Municipal. Read the full match report and roundup from the rest of the games here.

 Share 15h ago 03.19 EST Preamble
 Hello and welcome to matchday live!
 We have another big day of Nations League action after Norway overpowered Wales 3-1, Northern Ireland beat Ukraine 1-0 and Austria edged out Republic of Ireland 1-0 in yesterday’s fixtures.
 Today, England have the chance to finish top of their Nations League group if they can beat the world champions Spain. If Spain’s 3-2 victory over England in September is anything to go by, we’re in for a treat this evening. Defensive errors ultimately cost England in that game so they will need to be almost flawless to end Spain’s 43-match unbeaten run.
 Elsewhere, Chelsea beat Manchester City 1-0 in the Women’s Super League yesterday to go top of the table. There are three more WSL games this afternoon, including Arsenal v London City Lionesses.
 All of that and more to come. Stay tuned for updates.
